transcript: [00:00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh quick roll call from our side it's me maya and diego from redwood - and you are priya?
[00:00:10] Priya Nair: yes this is priya, thanks for doing this. we want to understand how your json mode can help our production routing needs
[00:00:21] Diego Alvarez: awesome, i'll try to focus on the runtime bits — decision graphs, how we route to different executors depending on latency/cost/quality
[00:00:35] Samir Patel: quick note we run a mix of real-time chat and batch email generation, p95 latency target for chat is 300ms and cost is a big driver

[00:00:48] Maya Chen: perfect. today's agenda: 1) quick console walkthrough for schema contracts 2) demo of a decision graph that routes to fast quantized model for short replies and to higher-quality model for long form 3) optimize recs for batching and quant 4) security Qs
[00:01:10] Evelyn Zhou: sounds good. also we're interested in on-prem options if needed, love to see how VPC or private works
[00:01:22] Diego Alvarez: cool, i'll jump into the console. note: some transcriber stuff may mislabel, sorry if names get swapped in the transcript

[00:01:35] [screen share start] Diego Alvarez: so here is the contract editor, you can define a typed schema for 'reply' with fields: intent, summary, actions[], confidence_score as float etc — we validate at runtime
[00:02:05] Priya Nair: do you support nested enums? we have hierarchy for categories

[00:02:15] Diego Alvarez: yes nested enums and unions, though larger schemas increase validation cost so we recommend pinning max fields — also you can toggle strict vs permissive validation in the route
[00:02:40] Maya Chen: important for reliability — strict mode rejects non-conforming responses and triggers fallback
[00:02:50] Samir Patel: fallback to what? do you have a model variant?

[00:02:58] Diego Alvarez: good q: fallback can be policy-driven: options are 1) rerun with a different prompt + same model, 2) route to a deterministic smaller model, 3) call a retriever or a tool. in our demo i'll show routing to a 'fast-quant' tier and then to 'high-qual' tier if confidence low
[00:03:25] Evelyn Zhou: and confidence is returned in the typed output?
[00:03:30] Diego Alvarez: yes it's part of the schema, can be used by the routing graph to make decisions — you can also plug in an evaluator step (small classifier) before routing

[00:03:50] [00:04:00] Diego Alvarez: here's a simple decision graph node: input->modelA (fast)->validate schema->if confidence < 0.7 then route to modelB (full), else return. you can also add cost thresholds
[00:04:30] Priya Nair: can the graph look at token budget or remaining quota? for example prefer cheaper path when budget low
[00:04:43] Maya Chen: yep policies can reference per-customer budget metrics, per-route SLOs, even region/affinity constraints
[00:04:55] Samir Patel: what about KV cache / prefix cache? chat context is heavy for us

[00:05:03] Diego Alvarez: we have automatic prefix/KV caching: if we detect repeated context we serve from cache, and caches are keyed by prompt fingerprint and model variant — Cache hits bypass model entirely which helps p95
[00:05:20] Evelyn Zhou: demo time please :)

[00:05:25] Diego Alvarez: ok i'll simulate a short chat prompt — modelA returns structured json quickly, validated, and the console highlights the contract fields; i'll intentionally cause schema violation next

[00:05:44] [00:06:00] Diego Alvarez: boom, invalid field type for confidence (string instead of float) — strict mode rejected; decision graph retried with a more constrained prompt and then routed to modelB; you can see fallback call and timing traces in the console
[00:06:30] Priya Nair: nice, the trace view will help debugging. how are these traces exposed to our observability?
[00:06:40] Diego Alvarez: exportable as spans to your tracing backend (OTel), and per-token cost/latency breakouts show on the route page
[00:06:55] Samir Patel: we need to ensure PII doesn't leak to any 3rd party, question around data residency and private deploy

[00:07:05] Maya Chen: understood; we have Private deployments (VPC, on-prem option). data stays in your network, integration with KMS/HSM for key control, and audit logs are retained per your retention policy
[00:07:20] Priya Nair: is SSO/SAML supported? we need SCIM+RBAC
[00:07:27] Maya Chen: yes SSO/SAML, SCIM for provisioning, RBAC at route and token level — i'll share the security pack after the call
[00:07:40] Evelyn Zhou: curious about Optimize recommendations — how would that apply to our mixed workload?

[00:07:47] Diego Alvarez: Optimize profiles analyze request histograms and suggest batching window, quantization profiles per model, and also when prefix caching will be effective — for your mixed chat+batch we often recommend small micro-batches for email gen and preserve low-latency path for chat with prefix caching
[00:08:10] Samir Patel: any example gains?
[00:08:14] Diego Alvarez: in similar customers we've seen 25-40% token cost reduction with moderate batching + 8-bit quantization on long-form, p95 improved by 10-15% due to caching
[00:08:30] [00:08:45] Priya Nair: I'd like to understand how canary rollouts work for schema changes — we have frequent contract iterations

[00:08:55] Diego Alvarez: you can do staged rollouts by route and model version, with automatic validation: if a new schema rejects more than X% of responses we auto-roll back. There's also a canary percentage and a 'dry-run' mode that logs violations without rejecting
[00:09:15] Maya Chen: and you can attach prompt test sets so regressions are detected in CI-like fashion
[00:09:23] Evelyn Zhou: one practical question: how do we compose tool calls? e.g., call an internal search API then pass results into a structured action

[00:09:33] Diego Alvarez: we support tool/function calling with typed I/O. you declare the function signature in the contract, the model returns the call object, runtime executes the call (or sandboxed), then the returned payload is validated against the schema and the graph proceeds
[00:09:50] Samir Patel: is runtime tool execution sandboxed? security is key for us

[00:09:55] Diego Alvarez: yes you can run tools in a sandbox, or mark them as safe to execute. for private deployments you can host the tool runner inside your VPC — runtime only passes allowed fields
[00:10:10] Priya Nair: about multi-tenant routing: we have internal teams with different SLAs, can we pin specific executors per tenant?
[00:10:18] Maya Chen: yes tenant-level policies, per-tenant quotas, and dedicated executor pools (reserved/dedicated) are supported — Redwood Dedicated option fits that use case
[00:10:35] Evelyn Zhou: a nit: sometimes transcripts here show wrong names; what is the best way for us to debug strange model outputs?
[00:10:44] Diego Alvarez: the console trace plus the request/response JSON is the first stop; you can rehydrate the exact context and replay locally or in sandboxed debug endpoints

[00:10:58] [00:11:15] Maya Chen: i'll flip to the Optimize tab — you can upload a sample traffic log and the optimizer suggests batching windows and quant profiles. it also predicts cost impact per route
[00:11:40] Samir Patel: can Optimize propose model substitutions automatically? like swapping to an L2 quantized variant when latency allows

[00:11:48] Diego Alvarez: yes suggestions include model substitution with confidence estimates; however we always recommend A/Bing in a controlled pilot — optimizer gives a projected delta not a forced change
[00:12:10] Priya Nair: on the pilot, timeline thoughts? we want a short POC to evaluate latency and quality

[00:12:19] Maya Chen: typical pilot: 4 weeks — week 1 on-boarding and traffic mirroring, week 2 run bench and collect metrics, week 3 apply Optimize recs and run A/B, week 4 review and finalize pricing
[00:12:36] Evelyn Zhou: costs during pilot?
[00:12:40] Maya Chen: pilots are usually subsidized; we'll include committed pricing options depending on expected qps; we'll put together a proposal after the benchmark
[00:12:55] Samir Patel: about legal: do you have standard DPA and data processing terms?
[00:13:02] Maya Chen: yes DPA, SOC2 and optional add-on for data residency controls — i'll include links in the security pack
[00:13:15] [00:13:30] Priya Nair: cross-checking: we need HSM/KMS integration for key management — is that part of Private?
[00:13:40] Diego Alvarez: available both for Private and Dedicated; for hosted we integrate to cloud KMS with customer-managed keys if needed
[00:13:55] Evelyn Zhou: any limitations around long token sequences and performance when using KV cache?

[00:14:03] Diego Alvarez: long sequences are handled by KV cache and attention optimizations; sequence length does impact memory but we have automatic kernel selection and can switch execution paths depending on length
[00:14:20] Maya Chen: okay i'll hand it back to priya for any blockers
[00:14:26] Priya Nair: two blockers: 1) security sign-off 2) seeing real traffic numbers in benchmark. If benchmarks show we can meet p95 and cost targets we'll move fast
[00:14:40] Maya Chen: totally reasonable — our deliverable is the benchmark and security pack
[00:14:46] Samir Patel: let's talk about error rates: what's the circuit breaker behavior when a downstream tool fails?
[00:14:53] Diego Alvarez: graph nodes can define retry/backoff, and you can configure fallbacks to degraded modes or to a safe default. we emit events to the console and to your webhook on failures
[00:15:12] Evelyn Zhou: can we set per-route SLA alerts?
[00:15:18] Maya Chen: yes alerts and automated rollback if SLA breaches cross thresholds, integrate with PagerDuty

[00:15:30] [00:15:50] Diego Alvarez: quick demo of a tool call: declared a function 'search_internal(query)->results[]', model returns call object, runtime executes search, returns JSON validated by schema, then model composes final reply — all visible in trace
[00:16:10] Priya Nair: what about controlling hallucination from tool outputs?
[00:16:15] Diego Alvarez: we validate tool outputs against schema and also have a verifier step — you can insert a deterministic checker or rerank results using an embedding similarity to source docs
[00:16:35] Maya Chen: one more: do you have support for per-token billing breakouts for showback?
[00:16:42] Diego Alvarez: yes token-level cost and latency breakdowns per request and aggregated per-route, available in Console and exported to billing reports
[00:16:58] Samir Patel: great. Priya any questions on the routing graph?
[00:17:05] Priya Nair: curious about edge cases: what if model returns valid schema but semantically wrong?

[00:17:12] Diego Alvarez: that's where quality checks and eval sets come in — you can attach small classifiers or use sampling-based human review; our rollout engine can measure quality regressions against held-out prompt sets
[00:17:30] Evelyn Zhou: the human-in-the-loop for high-risk queries is important for us
[00:17:35] Maya Chen: yep and you can configure routing so high-risk queries are flagged for manual approval or routed to deterministic toolchain

[00:17:50] [00:18:05] Maya Chen: okay i'm going to capture the pilot scope: 4-week pilot, mirror 5% production traffic, run 48h controlled benchmark, apply Optimize recs on week 3, then A/B and review
[00:18:25] Priya Nair: sounds good, please include expected infra needs and any network ports for VPC
[00:18:33] Diego Alvarez: will do — i'll include minimal network diagrams in the security pack
[00:18:45] Samir Patel: we may want to bring legal and security to the kickoff meeting; they usually want a technical readout first
[00:18:55] Maya Chen: agreed, we'll invite security/legal to the pilot kickoff. who should be on that invite from your side?
[00:19:02] Priya Nair: me and samir for sure, security lead tbd
[00:19:10] Evelyn Zhou: can you also share the console link and a short guide to the contract editor?
[00:19:16] Maya Chen: yes, guide + short video walkthrough, plus the security pack
[00:19:30] [00:19:45] Priya Nair: quick question about pricing: if we go dedicated, what's the lead time?
[00:19:52] Diego Alvarez: Dedicated pools commonly have a 4–8 week lead time depending on capacity and region, we'll include options in the proposal
[00:20:05] Samir Patel: any known limitations with binary attachments in tool calls? we pass small files
[00:20:13] Diego Alvarez: attachments are supported but for large binaries we recommend pre-signed URLs and a tool that pulls content, then runtime validates size and schema
[00:20:30] [00:20:45] Maya Chen: okay we're about halfway through, anything else on the tech side?
[00:20:52] Evelyn Zhou: one more on audit logs retention — we might need 7 years for compliance
[00:20:59] Maya Chen: long retention is an add-on, we can configure S3 buckets in your account for long-term logs
[00:21:12] Priya Nair: thanks. can you clarify the model catalog? which open models are verified?
[00:21:20] Diego Alvarez: we certify a subset of open models and maintain performance profiles; we also provide Redwood-verified quantized builds — full list in the docs I'll send
[00:21:35] Samir Patel: would you be able to run a quick smoke test against our sample dataset during the benchmark?
[00:21:42] Maya Chen: yes we'll run smoke and the 48h benchmark, and include JSON of all traces
[00:21:54] [00:22:10] Priya Nair: any questions about uptime SLA?
[00:22:16] Diego Alvarez: hosted API standard SLA is 99.9 for paid tiers, dedicated can be negotiated higher with reserved capacity
[00:22:28] Samir Patel: do you provide calendar-based maintenance windows?
[00:22:33] Maya Chen: yes configurable, and we can push notifications to your Slack/ops channels
[00:22:45] Evelyn Zhou: okay let's talk about the deliverables timeline again
[00:22:51] Maya Chen: recap: security pack by 9/30, Diego runs a benchmark and shares by 10/6, sample corpus by 10/1 from you, pilot kickoff week of 10/11 — tentative
[00:23:10] Priya Nair: can we accelerate the kickoff if benchmark looks good earlier?
[00:23:15] Maya Chen: absolutely, we can start earlier if both sides sign off
[00:23:25] [00:23:40] Diego Alvarez: small technical aside: if you embed routing logic in the prompt vs decision graph, debugging gets messy; we recommend graph-first for production
[00:23:58] Priya Nair: noted. any security concerns with embedding the decision graph config in our repo?
[00:24:05] Diego Alvarez: configuration can be stored in your repo and imported into the control plane; secrets are never stored in plain text, we recommend using parameter store
[00:24:20] Samir Patel: cross-region routing: our users are global — can you route by client geo?
[00:24:27] Maya Chen: yes geo-aware routing is supported with region affinity and fallbacks
[00:24:40] Evelyn Zhou: what about billing granularity per route/team?
[00:24:45] Diego Alvarez: per-route and per-token billing is available and exportable to your billing system, you can tag requests
[00:25:00] Priya Nair: okay i think we covered most things — any open technical risks?
[00:25:06] Diego Alvarez: main risk is model quality variance; we mitigate with evals, rollback and reranking steps; caching and batching strategy needs careful tuning but Optimize helps
[00:25:20] Maya Chen: for pilot we recommend a small QA loop and 1–2 human evaluators to sanity-check tooled outputs
[00:25:30] Evelyn Zhou: good. let's lock down the follow-up meeting
[00:25:36] Maya Chen: propose Oct 7 for the kickoff planning, is that good?
[00:25:43] Priya Nair: works for me
[00:25:47] Samir Patel: works here too
[00:25:52] [00:26:05] Maya Chen: great i'll send calendar invite and include security docs. any final questions?
[00:26:12] Priya Nair: none from me, appreciate the detailed demo
[00:26:18] Evelyn Zhou: likewise, thanks
[00:26:22] Diego Alvarez: thanks all, we'll follow up with docs and benchmark plan
[00:26:30] [00:26:45] End of recording (transcription continues with a short Q/A and some off-topic scheduling)
